name: Meadowcroft Rockshelter
hook: A Pennsylvania rockshelter with charcoal dates of up to 19,000 radiocarbon years, long before Clovis.
claim: James Adovasio's team argued that 11 well-defined strata at Meadowcroft Rockshelter record intermittent human occupation spanning at least 16,000 and perhaps 19,000 radiocarbon years -- long before Clovis.

claimed_age.label: 16,000-19,000 14C yr BP (uncalibrated)
claimed_age.basis: S1 (1978): the 11 strata 'span at least 16,000 years and perhaps 19,000 years.' Radiocarbon years (calibration did not then reach this range); not calibrated here. S16 (1977) already claimed 16,000.

accepted_age.label: Pre-Clovis by ~12,000-14,500 14C yr BP; older unconfirmed
accepted_age.basis: Conservative view ~12,000 yr (S7, citing Fagan 1995; units unstated). An independent 2025 synthesis (S14) uses 13,955-14,555 14C yr BP for lower Stratum IIa, following the excavators (S5). Uncalibrated.

orthodoxy_at_claim.label: Clovis-first: no accepted human presence in the Americas before Clovis (11,000-11,500 14C yr BP in S11; calendar limit 13,050 cal BP from S15)

unambiguous_signal.note: S1 reports occupation throughout the sequence, but critics questioned the 'character' of the earliest artifact assemblage (S7).

documented_context.note: 11 well-defined strata in a deeply stratified site (S1); critics nonetheless questioned the stratigraphy (S7).

multiple_dating_methods.note: Radiocarbon was the only dating method reported (50+ dates, S5); no second method appears in any source read.

multiple_labs.note: No source read names the lab(s) behind the 1970s dates; the only second-lab (Oxford AMS) dates cited came by 1990 (S5).

professional_recovery.note: Systematic excavation reported by professional archaeologists and specialists led by J.M. Adovasio (S1).

peer_reviewed_report.note: Full overview in American Antiquity in 1978 (S1), a year after the first report (S16).

material_accessible.note: No source read shows whether critics could examine samples or the site within about five years of the claim.

independent_teams.note: Within 1977-1982 the data came from the excavators (S1); critics' 1980 papers commented on those data (S3).

proponent_stake.note: Academic research; no commercial, religious or nationalist motive found in the sources read.

objections.text: Charcoal dates from the lowest strata may be too old because of particulate or non-particulate contamination by older carbon.
objections.outcome_note: Excavators rejected it using Oxford AMS dates (S5); S6 found no groundwater contamination. No source read reports a direct test for coal particles.

objections.text: Fauna and flora from dated Stratum IIa are discordant with other local Wisconsinan-age (full-glacial) fossils, casting doubt on the dates.
objections.outcome_note: Excavators replied that the dates are 'not discordant' with the associated fauna and flora (S12). No independent re-analysis was found.

objections.text: Early and perhaps some later dates may be contaminated by coal or dissolved coal by-products; the critics recommended specific tests to detect this.
objections.raised_by: Kenneth B. Tankersley; Cheryl Ann Munson
objections.outcome_note: Excavators replied there is 'no evidence whatsoever' of contamination (S13). No source read reports the recommended tests being done.

objections.text: Critics questioned the site's stratigraphy, on which the association of the earliest dates and artifacts depends (specific arguments not read here).
objections.raised_by: critics, as summarized by the excavators (S7)
objections.outcome_note: An independent 2025 study reports the dates in stratigraphic order (S14), but historic maize intruded into strata IV-XI (S9). No independent re-study of the lowest strata found.

objections.text: Critics questioned the 'character' of the earliest artifact assemblage (specific arguments not read here).
objections.raised_by: critics, as summarized by the excavators (S7)
objections.outcome_note: An independent 2025 study treats the lower Stratum IIa tools (26 tools, 298 debitage) as a coherent early blade-and-biface industry (S14); not yet a consensus.

status_note: Pre-Clovis use is accepted in an independent 2025 synthesis (S14); the excavators say even conservative views concede ~12,000 years (S7). The 16,000-19,000 14C-yr span is unconfirmed; S15 deems all pre-16 ka sites equivocal.
what_settled_it: Not settled. Oxford AMS dates (1990, S5) and micromorphology (1999, S6) answered some contamination concerns; an independent 2025 synthesis counts the site among 10 sites underpinning pre-Clovis technology (S14). No source read reports a test for coal, the main alternative.

timeline.event: Adovasio and colleagues publish a progress report calling Meadowcroft 'a 16,000 year chronicle'.
American Antiquity overview: the 11 strata span 'at least 16,000 years and perhaps 19,000 years' of occupation.
Haynes asks whether contamination is a problem for the site's early charcoal dates.
Mead argues the Stratum IIa fauna and flora are discordant with other local full-glacial fossils.
The excavators reply to Haynes and Mead that the dates fit the fauna, flora, artifacts and geology.
Tankersley, Munson & Smith show coal can contaminate radiocarbon samples and that standard lab procedures cannot remove it.
The excavators assess Oxford AMS dates and hold that people were present by 14,000-14,500 years ago.
Tankersley & Munson reiterate the coal-contamination concern; the excavators reject it for lack of evidence.
Goldberg & Arpin's micromorphology finds no evidence of groundwater contamination of the early levels.
Hart & Adovasio AMS-date maize from strata IV-XI to historic times (likely after AD 1800), showing intrusion in later strata.
Potter et al. regard all purported sites older than 16,000 cal yr BP as equivocal.
Madsen et al. (independent authors) count Meadowcroft among 10 sites underpinning pre-Clovis ('American Upper Paleolithic') technology.

decisive_tests.test: Single-fragment AMS dates on botanically identified charcoal from lower Stratum IIa features, run at an independent lab, with reflectance checks for coal on the same samples.
decisive_tests.would_show: Whether the oldest dates hold once coal particles, which standard lab pretreatment cannot remove (S17), are excluded.

decisive_tests.test: Screen archived charcoal and sediment from the deepest strata for coal particles by reflectance and paleobotanical analysis, compared with local coal seams.
decisive_tests.would_show: Direct evidence for or against coal contamination of the oldest dated samples.

decisive_tests.test: AMS-date any bone, antler or other non-charcoal organic material from the earliest strata.
decisive_tests.would_show: An independent material class to cross-check the charcoal-based chronology of the oldest levels.

decisive_tests.test: Desk study: compile all published Meadowcroft dates by stratum and lab number, calibrate them with IntCal20, and flag outliers and reversals.
decisive_tests.would_show: Calendar ages for the claimed and accepted occupations, and whether the basal dates are internally consistent.

falsifier: Toward 'refuted' only if all lower Stratum IIa dates prove contaminated (e.g., coal in dated charcoal) or intrusive. Toward 'vindicated' if single-fragment AMS dates on identified charcoal at an independent lab replicate the basal dates.

sources.citation: Adovasio, J.M., Gunn, J.D., Donahue, J. & Stuckenrath, R. 1978. Meadowcroft Rockshelter, 1977: An Overview. American Antiquity 43(4): 632-651.
sources.note: Original overview. Abstract read: 11 strata 'span at least 16,000 years and perhaps 19,000 years' of intermittent occupation.

sources.citation: Haynes, C.V. 1980. Paleoindian Charcoal from Meadowcroft Rockshelter: Is Contamination a Problem? American Antiquity 45(3): 582-587.
sources.note: Paywalled, no abstract; content not read. Title raises contamination; S5 and S7 summarize critics' claims as 'particulate or nonparticulate contamination'.

sources.citation: Mead, J.I. 1980. Is It Really That Old? A Comment about the Meadowcroft Rockshelter "Overview". American Antiquity 45(3): 579-582.
sources.note: Abstract read: Stratum IIa radiocarbon dates imply full-glacial occupation, but recovered fauna/flora are discordant with other local Wisconsinan-age fossils.

sources.citation: Tankersley, K.B. & Munson, C.A. 1992. Comments on the Meadowcroft Rockshelter Radiocarbon Chronology and the Recognition of Coal Contaminants. American Antiquity 57(2): 321-326.
sources.note: Abstract read: clarifies points of confusion about coal contamination of dated charcoal and recommends specific comparative tests.

sources.citation: Adovasio, J.M., Donahue, J. & Stuckenrath, R. 1990. The Meadowcroft Rockshelter Radiocarbon Chronology 1975-1990. American Antiquity 55(2): 348-354.
sources.note: Abstract read: critics assert 'particulate or nonparticulate contamination'; Oxford AMS dates assessed; people present 'by 14,000-14,500 years ago' (14C years).

sources.citation: Goldberg, P. & Arpin, T.L. 1999. Micromorphological Analysis of Sediments from Meadowcroft Rockshelter, Pennsylvania: Implications for Radiocarbon Dating. Journal of Field Archaeology 26(3): 325-342.
sources.note: Abstract read: deposition by attrition, roof fall and sheetwash; no evidence of groundwater contamination of the early levels. Does not test coal particles.

sources.citation: Adovasio, J.M., Pedler, D.R., Donahue, J. & Stuckenrath, R. 1999. Two Decades of Debate on Meadowcroft Rockshelter. North American Archaeologist 19(4): 317-341.
sources.note: Excavators' review. Abstract read: critics questioned stratigraphy, flora/fauna, assemblage 'character' and dates; 'most conservative assessments concede a 12,000-year initial occupancy'.

sources.citation: Kelly, R.L. 1987. A Comment on the Pre-Clovis Deposits at Meadowcroft Rockshelter. Quaternary Research 27(3): 332-334.
sources.note: Further published critique (title only; paywalled, no indexed abstract, not read).

sources.citation: Hart, J.P. & Adovasio, J.M. 2022. Accelerator Mass Spectrometry Dating of Meadowcroft Rockshelter Maize. Radiocarbon 64(2): 265-277.
sources.note: Full text read (open PDF). Site 'best known for its pre-Clovis occupation'; maize from strata IV-XI, once thought ancient, AMS-dates to historic times, most likely after AD 1800.

sources.citation: Waters, M.R. 2019. Late Pleistocene Exploration and Settlement of the Americas by Modern Humans. Science 365(6449): eaat5447.
sources.note: Abstract read: Americas settled ~17.5-14.6 ka; data 'do not support' earlier occupation. Background synthesis only.

sources.citation: Haynes, C.V. 1964. Fluted Projectile Points: Their Age and Dispersion. Science 145(3639): 1408-1413.
sources.note: Abstract read: Clovis points in sediments 'between 11,000 and 11,500 years old' (14C years); defines the Clovis-first view the claim challenged.

sources.citation: Adovasio, J.M., Gunn, J.D., Donahue, J., Stuckenrath, R. et al. 1980. Yes Virginia, It Really is That Old: A Reply to Haynes and Mead. American Antiquity 45(3): 588-595.
sources.note: Abstract read: Stratum IIa dates 'not discordant' with fauna, flora, artifacts or local geology; calls a 'Clovis primacy syndrome' anachronistic.

sources.citation: Adovasio, J.M., Donahue, J. & Stuckenrath, R. 1992. Never Say Never Again: Some Thoughts on Could Haves and Might Have Beens. American Antiquity 57(2): 327-331.
sources.note: Abstract read: says Tankersley & Munson 'reiterate' coal contamination; rejects it: 'no evidence whatsoever for particulate or nonparticulate contamination'.

sources.citation: Madsen, D.B., Davis, L.G., Williams, T.J., Izuho, M. & Iizuka, F. 2025. Characterizing the American Upper Paleolithic. Science Advances 11(43).
sources.note: Non-Adovasio authors. Passages read: Meadowcroft is one of 10 sites underpinning pre-Clovis technology; lower Stratum IIa 'between 13,955 and 14,555 radiocarbon years ago'.

sources.citation: Potter, B.A., Chatters, J.C., Prentiss, A.M., Fiedel, S.J. et al. 2022. Current Understanding of the Earliest Human Occupations in the Americas: Evaluation of Becerra-Valdivia and Higham (2020). PaleoAmerica 8(1): 62-76.
sources.note: Abstract read: Strict Clovis-First = 13,050 cal yr BP; all purported sites older than 16,000 cal yr BP 'equivocal'. Whether it discusses Meadowcroft is not known.

sources.citation: Adovasio, J.M., Gunn, J.D., Donahue, J. & Stuckenrath, R. 1977. Progress Report on the Meadowcroft Rockshelter—A 16,000 Year Chronicle. Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences 288(1): 137-159.
sources.note: Crossref metadata only (paywalled, no abstract). The title shows a 16,000-year chronology was public in 1977.

sources.citation: Tankersley, K.B., Munson, C.A. & Smith, D. 1987. Recognition of Bituminous Coal Contaminants in Radiocarbon Samples. American Antiquity 52(2): 318-330.
sources.note: Abstract read: coal is a demonstrated dating contaminant; standard lab procedures cannot remove it; paleobotanical and reflectance analyses detect it. Does not name Meadowcroft.

confidence_note: Haynes 1980 (S2), Kelly 1987 (S8) and the 1977 report (S16) were not read (paywalled, no abstract); Haynes' exact arguments, including any on coal, are unverified.
corrections: Brief says critics 'questioned the absence of Ice Age fauna.' The documented source of the fauna/flora objection is Mead (1980), unnamed in the brief, who calls them 'discordant' (S3); whether Haynes (1980) also made it is unverified.
notes: Two lines counted: radiocarbon dates; artifacts and features in stratified context (AMS is the same method; S6 tests integrity, not age). The excavators' 1980 reply decried a 'Clovis primacy syndrome' (S12), but no critic's text read here argues from Clovis-first, so no prior objection is coded. limit_bp is S15's Strict Clovis-First date, not a calibration of S11's 11,500 14C yr BP. The excavators' 14,000-14,500 figure (S5) is in 14C years; calibrated, it likely exceeds 16,000 cal BP (unsourced rough estimate), inside S15's equivocal class. Kelly 1987 (S8) and the Wheat 2012 opinion survey were not read; no survey figures are used.

open_issues: Clovis-first prior removed, not re-sourced: only the excavators allege it (S12, 'Clovis primacy syndrome'). Re-add, coded from the critic's own words, if Haynes 1980 (S2) is read and argues from Clovis-first.

year_claimed 1977 (S16, title only). S5 and S7 imply dates were published from 1975; a 1975 progress report (Pennsylvania Archaeologist 45(3), per the review) was not read. Use 1975 if it reports pre-Clovis dates.
limit_bp 13050 is S15's Strict Clovis-First date, not a calibration of 11,500 14C yr BP; sibling records code this orthodoxy as 13000 or 13350. Analyst should harmonize.
Status 'partial' rests on one independent synthesis (S14); S15 (abstract only) may class the site as equivocal. Recode 'open' if later independent reviews reject it.
multiple_labs recoded from 'no' to 'unknown': no source read names the lab(s) behind the 1970s dates.
Coal objection dated 1992, though S13 says the critics 'reiterate' it; S17 (1987) may be the first statement, but its abstract does not name Meadowcroft.
'identification' is a loose fit for the assemblage-'character' objection (schema: natural vs human-made); used as the nearest kind.
bp values kept null: individual lab dates not read or calibrated (see decisive test 4).
